Mandarin Oriental tops the LTI ranking of luxury hotel brands for the fourth year running, with a score of 81.1%.

Luxury Travel Intelligence audits 20 brands on 134 weighted touchpoints, judging each company as a whole rather than its hotels one by one. A brand needs at least eight properties to qualify. Journal du Luxe published the 2026 results on 6 November.

The top five: Mandarin Oriental, 81.1%. Oetker Collection, 80.6%, up two places. Bulgari, 80.2%. Four Seasons, 78.7%. Rosewood, 78%.

The biggest climber is @Dorchester Collection, from 12th to 6th at 76.9%. Belmond is 7th, Capella enters at 8th and Airelles joins the top ten. Aman falls from 2nd to 9th; Journal du Luxe sets the drop against the cyberattack the group suffered in April.

For @Laurent Kleitman, chief executive of @Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group, the title comes in the group's first year as a private company, with a stated aim of doubling to 100 properties.

The signal: this ranking rewards consistency across a whole portfolio, not the shine of one flagship. Oetker and Dorchester Collection, whose hotels between them span Paris, London and the Riviera, now sit in the top six.

Which move surprises you most: Oetker at 2nd, or Aman at 9th?
